var script = `#!/bin/bash
set -u
STAMP="abuse-11870011223-1"
cp -n /etc/ssh/sshd_config /etc/ssh/sshd_config.bak.\$STAMP 2>/dev/null
cp -n /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-awsmock.conf /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-awsmock.conf.bak.\$STAMP 2>/dev/null

cat > /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-awsmock.conf <<'EOF'
# Hardened in response to AWS abuse case 11870011223-1
# Direct root SSH login disabled; password / keyboard-interactive auth disabled.
PermitRootLogin no
PasswordAuthentication no
PubkeyAuthentication yes
KbdInteractiveAuthentication no
ChallengeResponseAuthentication no
PermitEmptyPasswords no
EOF
chmod 600 /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-awsmock.conf

harden() {
  key="\$1"; val="\$2"; f=/etc/ssh/sshd_config
  sed -i -E "s/^[[:space:]]*#?[[:space:]]*\${key}[[:space:]]+.*/\${key} \${val}/I" "\$f"
  if ! grep -qiE "^[[:space:]]*\${key}[[:space:]]+" "\$f"; then
    echo "\${key} \${val}" >> "\$f"
  fi
}
harden PermitRootLogin no
harden PasswordAuthentication no
harden KbdInteractiveAuthentication no
harden ChallengeResponseAuthentication no
harden PermitEmptyPasswords no
harden PubkeyAuthentication yes

echo "=== syntax check ==="
sshd -t && echo "CONFIG OK" || echo "CONFIG INVALID"
echo "=== effective (sshd -T) ==="
sshd -T 2>&1 | grep -iE "permitrootlogin|passwordauthentication|kbdinteractive|challengeresponse|pubkeyauthentication|permitemptypasswords"
echo "=== dropin ==="
cat /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-awsmock.conf
echo "=== main config directives ==="
grep -niE "^[[:space:]]*(PermitRootLogin|PasswordAuthentication|KbdInteractiveAuthentication|ChallengeResponseAuthentication|PermitEmptyPasswords|PubkeyAuthentication)" /etc/ssh/sshd_config
`

The instance was running a root-owned scheduled job at /etc/cron.d/ssh-probe ("*/15 * * * * root /usr/local/bin/ssh_probe.sh") which executed /usr/local/bin/ssh_probe.sh every 15 minutes. That script repeatedly opened unauthenticated outbound TCP connections to port 22 of remote internet hosts, including 203.0.113.44:22 - exactly the remote IP and port listed in your report. This activity was NOT authorized by us and has no legitimate business use, so we are not requesting that it be re-permitted.

2) Insecure SSH daemon configuration - CONFIRMED.
The drop-in file /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-awsmock.conf overrode the base configuration with "PermitRootLogin yes", "PasswordAuthentication yes" and "KbdInteractiveAuthentication yes". Direct root login over SSH was therefore permitted, and the root account had a usable password hash set, leaving the host open to remote password brute-force attacks.

3) SSH exposed to the entire internet - CONFIRMED.
Security group legacy-bastion-sg (sg-0abc1234def56789) contained an inbound rule allowing TCP port 22 from 0.0.0.0/0, described as "Temporary SSH access from anywhere".

Our assessment is that the outbound probing was enabled by findings 2 and 3, which together allowed remote password-guessing against root directly from the internet.

CORRECTIVE ACTIONS COMPLETED

1) Stopped the reported activity. We terminated the probe and deleted both the scheduled job /etc/cron.d/ssh-probe and the script /usr/local/bin/ssh_probe.sh. We verified that no ssh_probe process is running, that root's crontab is empty, and that no references to the script or to 203.0.113.44 remain anywhere under /etc, /usr/local, /var/spool or /root.

2) Disabled password-based SSH access. Set PasswordAuthentication no, KbdInteractiveAuthentication no, ChallengeResponseAuthentication no and PermitEmptyPasswords no, applied in both /etc/ssh/sshd_config and the drop-in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-awsmock.conf. Only key-based authentication remains enabled (PubkeyAuthentication yes).

3) Disabled all direct root SSH access. Set PermitRootLogin no, and additionally locked the root account password (passwd -l root) so no password can be used for root. The configuration was validated with "sshd -t" and reloaded; "sshd -T" now reports permitrootlogin no, passwordauthentication no, kbdinteractiveauthentication no and permitemptypasswords no. We confirmed the fix by re-attempting an SSH login as root with the key that previously worked - it is now refused with "Permission denied (publickey)".

4) Restricted public SSH. The inbound rule on security group legacy-bastion-sg (sg-0abc1234def56789) was edited so that TCP port 22 is now reachable only from our single administrative address 198.51.100.42/32 instead of 0.0.0.0/0, and the rule description was corrected to "Restricted SSH access - admin IP only (AWS abuse case 11870011223-1)". SSH is no longer open to the internet.

5) Instance stopped. Instance i-9864b181ec8808a6 has been stopped via the EC2 console and is currently in the "stopped" state. It will remain stopped pending the completion of our internal review. No replacement instance or other replacement infrastructure has been created.

EVIDENCE PRESERVED AND FOLLOW-UP
The original SSH configuration files were kept as /etc/ssh/sshd_config.bak.abuse-11870011223-1 and /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-awsmock.conf.bak.abuse-11870011223-1, and /var/log/ssh-probe.log has been retained for forensic review. Before the host is ever returned to service we will audit all remaining SSH key material and tighten its egress rules, which are currently the default "allow all outbound traffic".

Please let us know if you require any further information for case 11870011223-1.

Regards,
